We can search for templates matching functional group transformations: likely steps: 1) SN2 to attach side chain? The target has a side chain: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to N of triazine? Actually structure: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. Contains anisole ring with amide linking to a triazine (c2nnn...). The triazine has a substituent Cc3... (benzyl attached to heterocycle). That benzyl has a side chain CN4CC(F)C4 (a fluorinated azetidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-member? It's N4CC(F)C4: a morpholine? It's a N-azetidine with fluorine. So we need retrosynthesis: break amide (retro amide formation via condensation of amine and acid). Break C-N bond between benzyl and triazine (maybe SN2). Break Friedel-Crafts acylation to form anisole ring? Actually anisole ring attached to amide; could be formed via Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole with acyl chloride derived from triazine carboxylic acid? The forward reaction: Friedel-Crafts acylation attaches acyl group to aromatic ring, breaking halide (acyl chloride). So retro: remove acyl group to give anisole and acyl chloride (or acid). So step1: retrosynthetic disconnection of amide: target -> anisole (COc1cccc(NH) c1?) Actually anisole with amine? The amide bond between anisole amine (anilide) and carbonyl attached to triazine. So retro: break amide to give aniline (COc1cccc(NH2?) Actually the aniline would be COc1cccc(NH2) c1) and carboxylic acid derivative of triazine (C(=O)N...). So step1: amide disconnection.

Step2: break C-N bond between benzyl carbon and triazine nitrogen (the substituent Cc3...). That could be SN2 retro (i.e., substitution). The forward SN2 would be nucleophilic substitution of a halide (e.g., benzyl chloride) by triazine nitrogen. So retro: we need benzyl halide and triazine N-H? Actually the triazine nitrogen is attached to benzyl carbon via C-N bond. So retro: produce benzyl halide (e.g., benzyl chloride) and triazine with N-H (i.e., c2nnn(N)??). So step2: SN2.

Step3: Friedel-Crafts acylation to attach acyl group onto anisole? Actually forward Friedel-Crafts acylation attaches acyl onto aromatic ring, breaking halide (acyl chloride). So retro: remove acyl group from anisole to give anisole (methoxy phenyl) and acyl chloride (or acid). But we already used amide step; maybe the Friedel-Crafts is for attaching the amide carbonyl onto anisole? Wait Friedel-Crafts acylation attaches acyl group directly to aromatic ring, not amide. But our target has an amide attached to anisole via nitrogen, not carbonyl directly attached to ring. So maybe Friedel-Crafts is for installing the methoxy group? Actually methoxy is already there. Could be for installing the benzyl side chain onto phenyl? Not.

Maybe the three steps: 1) SN2 to attach the azetidine side chain onto benzyl chloride (i.e., forward SN2: CN4CC(F)C4 is nucleophile? Actually the side chain is CN4CC(F)C4 attached to benzyl via CH2-? The SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. That's a benzyl attached to N of azetidine via CH2-N. So forward SN2: benzyl halide reacts with N4CC(F)C4 (a secondary amine) to give benzyl-amine. So retro: break C-N bond to give benzyl halide and azetidine amine.

2) Friedel-Crafts acylation to attach the triazine carbonyl onto anisole? Actually the amide is formed via condensation, not Friedel-Crafts. Maybe Friedel-Crafts is for attaching the triazine onto benzyl? Not.
